answers.rationale: Ansor's core: subgraph-level sketch generation, learned cost model, subgraph prioritization by end-to-end contribution; removes per-op manual templates while remaining tractable.
Gap 0.42 vs 0.44/0.45 (~0.02-0.03 ms) is same order as measurement std (0.03 ms); noise dominates. Fix: more reps + robust statistic / equivalence band.

A one-off must not spend hours tuning. B recompile-per-shape inflates effective budget. D long-tail serving amortizes tuning. C false — tuning determines the artifact quality, so it does affect serving latency.
Folding: mul 2,3 -> const 6. CSE: t3,t4 syntactically identical -> single value. DCE: %unused pure and dead -> removed. All three preserve semantics.
B register spill unpredictable from op counts. C cache/TLB noise. D warmup/JIT/clock ramp. A false — static model uses simplified assumptions, divergence is inherent.
Vertical=producer-consumer merge along dataflow; horizontal=independent ops sharing input/launch dims; epilogue=lightweight pointwise attached to heavy compute (e.g., GEMM+bias+GELU).

Fusion is semantically legal, but T is still needed by Z. If T remains materialized, fused kernel re-executes f inside the reduction loop while Z reads original T => compiler duplicates compute or forgoes fusion.

A device boundary requires explicit copy. B in-place mutation with alias violates ordering. C rank/extent mismatch challenges common loop nest. D graph-output materialization is required. E false (FP32 fusion is common). F false (pointwise-pointwise fusion is a canonical case).
Traffic benefit needs the GEMM to expose an epilogue slot writing per-tile output only after applying pointwise chain in registers; otherwise pointwise ops still read/write full M×N via DRAM.
96 regs/thread + 48B/thread spills + 25% occupancy => spill-driven local memory traffic exceeds DRAM saved by not materializing intermediate. Classic fusion regression.
Same algorithm admits many schedules with vastly different perf; separation lets exploration without breaking correctness; portability across CPUs/GPUs/DSPs via rescheduling.
Log explicitly states reason: fusion would force reduction to broadcast pointwise input, >2× traffic; heuristic treats added memory traffic as fusion cost.
Kernel selection = per op instance choose implementation (library / generated / fused) based on op-type, shape, dtype, layout, hw; optionally cost-model ranked.
NHWC places channel as fastest-varying, matches Tensor Core / im2col tile access; NCHW has channel as strided outer axis unsupported by many TC kernels.
B relieve register pressure. C enable vectorization of part. D different tiling per half. A false — if already fits in L1 with reuse, fissioning hurts by touching intermediates twice.
Fused body reads B[i+1] which is produced by iteration i+1 of the original producer loop; in iteration i of the fused loop this hasn't happened yet. Flow dependence violated.
Compile-time lifetime analysis + non-overlapping lifetime tensors share underlying buffer; static allocation plan runtime executes without per-op malloc/free.

A manual templates don't generalize. B learned cost model beats pure analytical. C sketch-based space structuring for evo search. D false (real measurement is still needed). E false (with equivalent budget MetaSchedule can match/exceed).
A reduction associativity needed. C no output dep. D no true/anti dep. B false — branches within loop body are fine as long as inter-iteration deps satisfied.

A baseline choice matters. C need per-target tuning. D 'portability' = framework can generate good schedules, not one artifact everywhere. B false (TC utilization % across targets doesn't equal fairness if algorithms differ).

A memory-limited batch/context growth pays off. B cheap-op big-activation is favorable. E selective per-op checkpointing wins. C false (compute-bound with small activation = little to save). D false (numerics preserved; recomputation is deterministic replay).
ikj: inner j walks B[k,:] (unit stride) and writes C[i,:] (unit stride). A[i,k] hoisted as scalar-in-inner-loop. Better spatial locality than ijk which strides B by N.
Canonical contrast: AutoTVM = fixed template + parameter search; Ansor = template-free generation from tensor expression via schedule primitives, no manual template but larger space.

A specialization enables constant-based opts. B dynamic-shape trades some perf for compile time / storage. E bucketed hybrid strategy. C false (one-shot shapes lose compile time benefit). D false (dynamic-shape is semantically correct, not numerically wrong).

1024/128 = 8 blocks in each dim => 8*8=64 blocks? No — actually the grid at 1024/128 = 8x8 = 64 blocks. But profile says '8 blocks' — likely they mean per-dim or the grid is 1D. In any case, ~24 SMs idle on A100 confirms parallelism bottleneck. 64x64 tile gives 256 blocks, all SMs busy.
Transfer works when features match (same op class + same hw). Cross op-class (GEMM->Conv) and cross-hw (A100->H100) break feature applicability.

B split is a pure iteration-space refactor. C reorder requires dep-preserving check. D vectorize requires no cross-iter deps + compatible vector width. A false — bind requires legality checks; not every loop is safe to bind to blockIdx.x.
Tight loop where overhead already fits in one issue slot; 8× unroll triples code size, evicts I-cache, slows surrounding function.
Loop is vectorizable — A[i-1] is a read, not a write, and B/C[i] have no cross-iter write deps. Compiler needs an unaligned/shifted load for A[i-1] and tail block for N mod 8 != 0.
